## Adversarial Review Findings — Story 2.2 Seat Selection Diff

- **Selection state is a dead end in the UI.** `booking.html` still renders `<aside class="booking__summary"></aside>` completely empty. A user can toggle any number of seats but there is no summary, running count, price, or "weiter/continue" affordance anywhere — the feature lets you pick seats and then gives you nowhere to go with that choice.

- **`BookingSelectionService` performs no domain validation.** `toggle()`/`isSelected()` blindly trust whatever `rowLabel`/`columnNumber` they're given. Nothing in the service checks the value against the current `SeatMap` (existence, or that the cell is actually `status === 'free'`). The only thing stopping an occupied/aisle cell from being "selected" is that `seat-map.html` happens to only wire `(click)="onToggle(...)"` inside the `free` branch — a purely template-level guard, not a service-level invariant.

- **No maximum-selection limit.** Nothing prevents a user from selecting every free seat in the venue. For a real booking flow this is almost certainly wrong (most ticketing UIs cap selectable seats per order), and it's unclear from the diff whether this is deliberately deferred or simply missed.

- **Zombie selections if the seat map ever changes underneath the user.** If a selected seat's status later flips to `occupied` (concurrent booking by someone else, future polling/websocket refresh, etc.), the cell silently falls out of the `free` template branch, but the entry stays in `BookingSelectionService.selectedSeats()` forever — invisible in the UI yet still counted by anything that later reads `selectedSeats()` (e.g. a price total or submit payload).

- **`providers: [BookingSelectionService]` is scoped to a component whose constructor never reacts to route param changes.** `BookingPage`'s constructor reads `route.snapshot.paramMap` once. Angular's default route-reuse strategy reuses the same component instance when navigating between two `/booking/:id` routes with different ids, so a same-instance navigation from event A to event B would neither refetch the new seat map nor reset the selection service — stale seat picks from event A could remain "selected" against event B's grid. The seat-map staleness bug predates this diff, but attaching persistent selection state to the same lifecycle compounds the blast radius.

- **Repeated linear scans per cell per change-detection cycle.** Each free cell binds `isSelected()` four times directly (`[class.seat-cell--free]`, `[class.seat-cell--selected]`, both icon class bindings) plus once more inside `ariaLabel()` — five `.some()` scans over the whole selection array per cell, per CD tick. For a venue with hundreds of seats and a non-trivial selection count this is an easily avoidable inefficiency (e.g. a `Set<string>` or a single memoized `computed()`).

- **No `aria-pressed`/`aria-selected` on the toggle button.** Selection state is communicated only by rewriting the `aria-label` text from "frei" to "ausgewählt". That's functional, but it's a non-idiomatic pattern for a toggle control inside a `role="gridcell"`, where `aria-selected` is the conventional mechanism — worth confirming this was a deliberate a11y call rather than an oversight.

- **`selectedSeats()` ordering is toggle-order, not seat order.** Deselecting and reselecting a seat re-appends it at the end of the array instead of preserving its original position. Nothing documents or tests this ordering guarantee (or lack of one), so any future summary/list UI built on `selectedSeats()` will silently inherit "last-toggled-last" order unless someone notices and re-sorts.

- **No regression test pins that non-free cells can never become selectable.** The `onToggle` binding only exists on the `free` branch today, but there's no test asserting that clicking/activating an `occupied` cell is a no-op — that invariant is currently protected only by template structure, not verified behavior.

- **No test verifies the per-page provider scoping actually isolates state.** The whole "component-scoped service" design rests on `providers: [BookingSelectionService]` in `booking.ts`, but nothing tests that two separately created `BookingPage`/`SeatMapGrid` instances get independent `BookingSelectionService` instances rather than accidentally sharing one via a hoisted provider.

- **Magic-number checkmark CSS with no token backing.** `.seat-cell__icon--check` (`width: 10px`, `height: 5px`, `margin-top: -2px`, `rotate(-45deg)`) is a hand-tuned border-trick checkmark sized against the existing 12×12 `--seat` icon box, but unlike the surrounding colors (which use CSS custom properties), none of these dimensions are tokenized. Any future change to `--seat-cell-size` or the icon box will likely misalign it with nothing catching it except manual visual QA.

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings into a common format. Expected input formats:

   - Edge Case Hunter: JSON array with `location`, `trigger_condition`, `guard_snippet`, `potential_consequence` fields

   If a layer's output does not match its expected format, attempt best-effort parsing. Note any parsing issues for the user.

   Convert all to a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- `blind`, `edge`, `auditor`, or merged sources (e.g., `blind+edge`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** If two or more findings describe the same issue, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer edge-case JSON with location over adversarial prose).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind+edge`).

3. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

4. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.

   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.

+
+- [x] [Review][Defer] Auswahlstate bleibt bei Routenwiederverwendung zwischen zwei Buchungsstrecken erhalten (kompoundiert vorbestehende Seatmap-Staleness aus Story 2.1) [seed-a-frontend/src/app/features/booking/booking.ts:26-32] — deferred, pre-existing. `BookingPage` liest die Routen-Id weiterhin nur einmalig im Konstruktor (bereits in `deferred-work.md` aus Story 2.1 dokumentiert und in dieser Story unter AD-6-Notiz als `[ANNAHME]` bestätigt). +Automatisierte Review-Layer (Blind Hunter, Edge Case Hunter, Acceptance Auditor) haben zusätzlich folgende Punkte aufgeworfen; nach Prüfung gegen Spec/Architektur/bestehende Tests als Rauschen bzw. bereits abgedeckt eingestuft (kein Actionable-Finding):
+  - Leeres `.booking__summary` (kein Preis/Weiter-Button) — explizite Scope-Grenze dieser Story, siehe Dev Notes (Story 2.4/2.5).

+  - Kein `aria-pressed`/`aria-selected` auf der Sitzplatz-Zelle — bewusste, in der Story dokumentierte `[ANNAHME]` (Rolle ist auf `gridcell` überschrieben, Zustand wird stattdessen über `aria-label` kommuniziert).
+  - Reihenfolge von `selectedSeats()` folgt der Auswahlreihenfolge, nicht der Sitzreihenfolge — aktuell kein Konsument, der eine Sortierung erwartet.
+  - Fehlender expliziter Test „Klick auf belegt/Gang wirkungslos" — strukturell bereits durch bestehende Story-2.1-Tests abgedeckt (disabled-Buttons bzw. keine Button-Handler auf Gang-Zellen).
+  - Fehlender Test für Provider-Scope-Isolation zwischen zwei `BookingSelectionService`-Instanzen — testet Angular-DI-Verhalten, nicht Anwendungslogik.
+  - Magic-Number-Werte in `.seat-cell__icon--check` (SCSS) ohne Design-Token — konsistent mit dem bereits bestehenden Muster von `.seat-cell__icon--lock` in derselben Datei.
+  - `SelectedSeat` dupliziert `rowLabel`/`columnNumber` statt einen mit `SeatMapCell` geteilten Identitäts-Typ zu nutzen — entspricht der bindenden Consistency Convention „Sitzplatz-Identifikation" (zwei Felder, keine kombinierte Form); verfrühte Abstraktion für eine einzelne Duplizierung.
+  - Kein optionaler Fallback bei `inject(BookingSelectionService)` — beabsichtigtes AD-6-Design (routen-/komponenten-gescopter Provider, kein globales Singleton); ein `NullInjectorError` bei fehlendem Provider ist das gewünschte, laute Fail-Fast-Verhalten.
